chapter: Navy years and attitudes toward whites
title: Combat and skirmishes on Okinawa
summary: Protecting supplies from the Japanese, shooting at people, and turning back from a sniper hunt on Sugar Hill.

blocks.x: And, boy, there was, well, I didn't actually do no, but it was all around.

Everybody hit the ground. And, you know, I was like, no, on day. And so what we had to do was get the supplies off the ship, protect them. Because they were, well, we did, we had skirmishes with the Japanese who were trying to come in to get the food or whatever, and we had to protect them from that. So it was always a skirmish. I shot at people and I don't know if I killed nobody. Oh, okay, so you, yeah.
But you never really had any hand-to-hand combat?

No, no, hand-to-hand combat. Now I tell you what I did though, see they had, they had, when we secured Okinawa, they had 80,000 Japanese up in the hills, see, and the Marines used to guard this, they called it Sugar Hill. The Marines would guard around the bottom and anybody can volunteer to go and hunt snipers, I recall. And one day I volunteered. And we got a truckload of us. And when we got, you know, you volunteer if you want, you come back. When I got to the bottom of that hill and the Marines said, guard is just up in the hills up there, boy. He said, when you get on up there by the block up, you're on your own. I came back. I got off the truck and then I got back on the truck. Because I made a vow. I said, I'm here, I'm so far from home, I said, I'm going to go back home. And I made it back. I know one friend, I can say this, one friend of mine, he was lost on Okinawa, nobody, they never found him. He disappeared. And they found no remains. That's the truth.
